abstract: Charlotte Walker-Osborn, Commercial Partner and TMT Sector Head, and Nisha Patel, Trainee Solicitor, both of Eversheds LLP, give us an update on cybersecurity.
Aladdin Ayesh, CEng, FBCS, reader in artificial intelligence at De Montfort University, examines the subject of socially augmented environments and immersive simulators.

articleTitle: Ubiquitous Computing Riding the Next Wave
abstract: The term ubiquitous computing has been used since the late 1980s, referring to the spread of computing into almost any device in any location, in the home and the workplace. It has been an important concept, but is now becoming directly relevant to the way most of our technology works. Mark Say, author of BCS's new paper ‘Riding the Next Wave: Ubiquitous Computing,’ explains more.

articleTitle: State of Play Report BYOD, CYOD, BYOT, BYOA and MORE

abstract: The idea of cyber wargames usually conjures up a vision of large numbers of staff faced by a developing crisis shown in glorious multimedia and managed by a huge team of umpires. Whilst such large exercises are necessary for government level wargames, it is quite possible to run an effective business cyber wargame with very modest resources says John Curry.

articleTitle: The Search for Little Green Men
abstract: The risk equation has two components; likelihood and consequence. The consequence is pretty much an absolute one, in that we can reasonably anticipate the outcome, but the likelihood is pretty much a guess, says John Mitchell.

Peter Harris FBCS CITP is an information privacy consultant and currently chair of the BCS Information Privacy Expert Panel. He explains about the revised version of the Personal Data Guardianship Code.
Leron Zinatullin says that one way to tackle threats from inside your organisation is understand who they are.
In the Spring 2014 ITNOW Alex Reilly MBCS wrote about Alan Turing's computational oracle. This piece is intended to indicate the bases of computational and oracle systems in a broad sense.
Data loss, or breach, may be caused by three things: accident, deliberate attack or negligence says John Mitchell.

Justin Whatling, Chair BCS Health, and Luke Readman, Vice Chair Strategy & Policy BCS Health, examine the gap between the NHS trusts that are ambitious to deliver paperless healthcare and those that are lagging behind.

The Identity Assurance Working Group has been making inputs on cybersecurity and internet identity assurance to the UK and UN Internet Governance Forum (IGF) on behalf of BCS for the last four years. Louise Bennett FBCS reports.
The following papers are from The Computer Journal, issues 4 to 7, Volume 57, 2014. The overviews are largely based on the abstracts. They are provided by Editor-in-Chief, Prof. Fionn Murtagh.

articleTitle: Treating PTSD and PHOBIAS and MORE
abstract: Interacting with Computers looks at the importance of inducing anxiety and associated physiological arousal in virtual environments. Brian Runciman MBCS reports.

In recent years, the post-compulsory sector (specialist sixth form colleges and further education colleges) has begun to experiment with the concept of using data amassed about a student to provide targeted one-to-one coaching for success. Megan Robertson FBCS CITP explains how it works.
This paper in Interacting with Computers says that personal information management can be improved without radical paradigms.
Service management is becoming an important issue for many companies. With this in mind Henry Tucker MBCS spoke to Luis Soares from TOPdesk to find out what the issues are.
Gareth Baxendale FBCS, Head of Technology, Clinical Research Network, at the National Institute for Health Research, discusses all things technology-related in the healthcare arena.

articleTitle: Left of the Inside Back Cover
To Share or Not to Share
abstract: With a medically-orientated menagerie of clinicians, health informaticians and software suppliers meeting at HC2014, it wasn't long before BCS Health Editor, Justin Richards MBCS, realised what was foremost on almost everyone's mind, namely care.data.

Does the IT function understand business requirements? Does the business understand the potential impacts of its needs? The idea of an ‘IT linguist’ to smooth the communication paths is recorded here by Brian Runciman MBCS, based on the BCS debate ‘The IT team of the future.’

articleTitle: What Digital Leaders Say… 2014 and Beyond
abstract: What management issues and IT trends are being prioritised in the near and mid-term future by digital leaders? What additional resources, if any, are needed? Brian Runciman MBCS looks at the latest BCS Digital Leaders survey – now in its third year - to assess the strategic needs of the IT nation.

articleTitle: State of Play Report: Apps: Development, Deployment, Security and More

abstract: Alan Turing needs little introduction as a pioneer of computer design, software and as the originator of the theory of computation. Alex Reilly MBCS looks at Turing's computational oracle.
Peter Singleton considers the application of autonomy to what are commonly called ‘secondary uses’ of healthcare data.
Alan Freeland FBCS CITP, who has worked extensively in the Middle East, explains some of the ethical issues that arise from doing business in other parts of the world.
Kevin Linsell MBCS, Head of Service Development, Adapt, asks when it comes to the cloud, should businesses put all their efforts into just one basket?
Brandt Dainow MBCS CITP, Consultant at ThinkMetrics examines the ethical issues that need to be addressed as the IT industry develops new products over the next 10 to 15 years.
Gareth Niblett, Chairman of the BCS Information Security Specialist Group, says there will always be errors - it's how you deal with them.

A central function of BCS Council is that it provides advice to the Trustee Board on the direction and operation of BCS, The Chartered Institute for IT, explains Council Vice-Chair Kevin Streater FBCS CITP.
John Mitchell spends a lot of time reviewing risk registers. He finds it an amusing adjunct to his job as anIS auditor.

Martin Webster MBCS CITP is managing solution architect at Leicestershire County Council and his job is to solve problems, find solutions that enable beneficial business-led change. Project management is a core competence in directing and managing change.

3D printing is one of the hottest things at the moment yet it still doesn't have that killer use just yet. To get a better idea of what it is and what it can do, Henry Tucker MBCS met with Christopher Elsworthy from Bristol-based company Robox.

Augmented reality is a buzzword at the moment and the commercial world is already running full steam ahead with the technology. With that in mind, Judy Bloxham, eLearning Advisor, Jisc RSC Northwest, explores how augmented reality is making a difference to the learning process.

articleTitle: How Many Project Managers Does it Take to Send a Tweet?
abstract: The technology world has changed massively in recent years, but how much has project management changed and how have project managers changed the way they work? Jonnie Jensen, social business strategist and founder of Live And Social, looks at what it is going to take for more project managers to confidently go social.
David Reynolds, Chair of the PROMS-G, the specialist group for project and programme management, explains the role of the group and its various activities.
Eri Takahashi is the founder of EcoHarvester and she created the Bonsai Light. She spoke to Henry Tucker about it.
Andy Smith FBCS CITP provides an update on the Security Community of Expertise (SCoE).

Paul Excell is the Chair of BCS Entrepreneurs, a group with over 400 members that provides advice, guidance and mentoring to entrepreneurs who are sole traders, in small companies and even large corporations. He spoke to Henry Tucker MBCS about the group and the environment for startups in the UK.
IT consultant Paul Hula spoke to Justin Richards MBCS about the current state of programming and his work in health informatics.

Ian Drew is Chief Marketing Officer and EVP Business Development of ARM, the British semiconductor intellectual property supplier. He spoke to Henry Tucker about challenges for the company and the IT industry over the next 12-18 months.
Gareth Niblett, Chairman of the BCS Information Security Specialist Group, says data loss prevention is about sharing information securely.
Richard Piggin examines the cyber threats to industrial control systems (ICSs) and SCADA (supervisory control and data acquisition).
Gareth Niblett, Chairman of the BCS Information Security Specialist Group, examines risk and how we can deal with it.

The smart home might sound like something out of science fiction but it is rapidly becoming a reality. Henry Tucker spoke to Cees Links Founder and CEO of GreenPeak a company that develops chips for connected home devices.

We tend to take electronic communications for granted. Like power and water it's always there, but although it's a part of the critical national infrastructure (CNI), this doesn't mean it can't or doesn't fail from time to time says David Sutton.
Louise T. Dunne, Managing Director of Auriga, looks at the failings of the information security sector and asks if there is a better way.
Chris Tucker FBCS explores the nature of the insider threat in the digital age and mulls over the difficult balance of freedom of access with protecting information.

articleTitle: State of Play Report Augmented Reality in the Enterprise

abstract: Roger Cook MBCS CITP provides a cautionary tale that highlights one of the many risks to modern businesses.

articleTitle: Fail to Prepare Prepare to Fail
abstract: Operational information security is arguably the most complicated, confusing and, at times, stressful area of the IT profession to work in, says Adam Wood, a security analyst in the utility industry.

Rob Pritchard MBCS says that although there are have been some new security challenges in the past year, good asset management means that companies can assess the problems quickly and plan accordingly.

Professor Liz Bacon FBCS CITP CEng as the current BCS President is championing two key themes: transforming education through technology enhanced learning, and inspiring more women to choose computing as a career.

articleTitle: I, Business Analyst Reply on ‘The IT Linguist’
abstract: Julian Fletcher MBCS CITP CEng writes in response to reading the article ‘The IT Linguist’ which appeared in Summer 2014 ITNOW and the accompanying video debate ‘The IT team of the future webinar’ by the BCS expert panel at: www.bcs.org/itfuture
When it comes to IT security there are lessons that can be learned from the pharmaceutical world, says Pete Boyall.

The area of risk assessments and risk management are critical to all walks of life and there are various formal processes that are available for performing risk assessments and managing risk says Andy Smith FBCS CITP.

A quiet revolution is underway in IT apprenticeships, one in which government, employers, professional bodies and awarding bodies are aligned. Paul Jagger FBCS, reports.
The following papers are from The Computer Journal, issues 8 to 11, Volume 57, 2014. The overviews are largely based on the abstracts. They are provided by Editor-in-Chief, Professor Fionn Murtagh.

Surprising at it may seem no computer or robot has yet been charged with a crime, let alone convicted, or punished or brought to justice in any other fashion, says Paul Jagger FBCS CITP, Secretary of the BCS Learning and Development Specialist Group.
The January issue of Interacting with Computers publishes a study of behaviour inside a virtual world when the aim is to collaborate rather than play. Brian Runciman MBCS reports.
Vice-Chair Kevin Streater FBCS CITP reports on the latest BCS Council meeting.
The following papers are from The Computer Journal, issues 2 and 3, Volume 57, 2014. The overviews are largely based on the abstracts. They are provided by Editor-in-Chief Prof. Fionn Murtagh.

Almost every job relies on some aspect of technology whether it's sitting at a PC in an office, working at a checkout or delivering parcels. Richard French of BCS, The Chartered Institute for IT, looks at digital literacy as an employability skill.

Robots offer a unique insight into what people want from technology. They also pose serious questions about ethics and regulation of identity and the internet of things. I mind about this topic in a very real sense because I expect robots to help me as I get older, says Louise Bennett Chair of the BCS Security Community of Expertise.
In the rush to extend the reach of IT to more and more new fields of application, it seems we may be neglecting to ask some fundamental questions says Don Southey MBCS.

Alison Holt, BCS author of Governance in IT and expert in corporate governance of IT and sustainability management, says that with software all around us we need to know if it's ethically fit-for-purpose.
A revolution in computing at schools starts in September 2014, says BCS Deputy President Liz Bacon. It aims to make all schools excel at teaching computing.

All computers talk; whether it be your laptop, tablet, mobile phone or smart TV, you may never have heard them speak but they have a voice, says Giacomo F. Mosca FBCS, Senior Director, Technical Operations, Transparent Technology

Gary Lloyd posed the question ‘what proportion of IT-based projects deliver what they say they would, on time and on budget?’ at meetings of three different consultancy, project/programme management and business change BCS specialist groups. Most of the attendees were, like Gary, of mature years and had seen a lot of projects.
At CES2014 Henry Tucker spoke to Dan Cui from Vuzix about the company's rival product to Google Glass and the issues surrounding wearable computing.

Who would be a CISO? Ensuring security has never been easy, but CISOs are now facing an unprecedented series of challenges, the combination of which is creating a near-unmanageable situation for security professionals. Duncan Brown FBCS asks what has gone wrong, and how can we fix it?
Council update on the strategic plan 2014 as reported by Vice-Chair Kevin Streater FBCS CITP.
One of the big themes at CES2014 was around technology that is being included in cars. Henry Tucker MBCS got hands-on with tech from three car giants.
John Doody FBCS CITP asks if you would leave your house unlocked when you go to work.
Vice-Chair Kevin Streater FBCS CITP reports on the November BCS Council meeting.
Ian Herbert, Committee Member, BCS Primary Healthcare Specialist Group (PHCSG) and BCS Health Executive takes a close look at Care.data.

Bob Hughes is the Event Coordinator of the BCS Project, Programme and Portfolio Management Specialist Group. He is a Principal Lecturer at the University of Brighton and is editor of BCS publication Project Management for IT-related Projects and also of Exploiting IT for Business Benefit.
Tony Anscombe is a senior security evangelist from AVG Technologies. He spoke to Henry Tucker about staying safe online and mobile malware.

Ian Merricks is Program Director for Fast Forward (FFWD) London, a three-way partnership with Accelerator Academy, City University London and match funding from the EU ERDF (European Regional Development Fund).
When it comes to dealing with security threats we need to be constantly vigilant says Gareth Niblett, Chairman of the BCS Information Security Specialist Group.
Interacting with Computers has run a special issue on use of sensors and recognition technology in learning environments. Brian Runciman MBCS reports.

BCS, The Chartered Institute for IT, recently held a summit for and about digital leaders. Included in the summit was a discussion session about the role of the chief information officer (CIO) hosted by Ade McCormack and featuring Nick Millman from Accenture, John Morton from IP<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and Dave Wheeldon from Aveva.

Whirlpool has developed a concept, creating a one kitchen console with a cook anywhere surface where you are able not only to cook, but also juggle the rest of life and enhance the multi-tasking experience. Henry Tucker stepped into the kitchen.
John Mitchell has been re-reading Sun Tzu's The Art of War. ‘Know thy enemy’ is the mantra chanted at all military colleges, but it is only part of the quotation.

Gustav Metzger is an artist with a socially-engaged conscience who has become famous for hisconcepts of auto-destructive and auto-creative art. Always cognisant of the latest technologicaldevelopments, he has had an association with the Computer Arts Society from the early days. At hisexhibition Lift Off! previously on view in Cambridge we learned his ‘processes of transformation […]offer powerful metaphors for revolution and transcendence.’ (From the accompanying catalogue).

articleTitle: Crossing the Event Horizon of the IoT
abstract: The popular view of the internet of things (IoT), insofar as it has penetrated the public awareness, seems to veer between utopian visions of robot-chauffeured cars and 24/7 health monitoring to a fear that we may be sleepwalking into Orwell's 1984, albeit 30 years late. Brian Runciman MBCS looks at a recent BCS survey on the IoT.

Charlotte Walker-Osborn, Partner and Head of Eversheds LLP's Tech, Media and Telecoms Sector and Ben McLeod, Commercial and Information Technology Group, Eversheds LLP, take a look at a handful of the key developments in IT and data law and related trends for 2014.

articleTitle: Judgement on Drones Robots Ethical Decision Dilemmas
abstract: They could detect forest fires, fly medication into battle fields, assist in archaeological digs, aid police surveillance for benign reasons, control effective crop spraying, monitor or undertake rescue attempts in hazardous environments they could be used for uncontrolled automatic warfare, aid police surveillance for less than benign reasons, snoop and generally infringe civil liberties and privacy. Brian Runciman MBCS reports.

articleTitle: Ladies and Gents these are the Numbers
abstract: Whilst many of the headline figures for 2014's report are still negative there are some points of optimism in the thorny issue of gender diversity in IT. E-skills and BCS, The Chartered Institute for IT have updated their scorecard for gender representation in the IT industry – a robust and rigorous exposition of an issue that still surprises in the 21st century. Brian Runciman MBCS reports.

Index Terms: Information And Communication Technology In Education

abstract: Eversheds LLP's Head of Tech, Media and Telecoms, Charlotte Walker-Osborn, speaks to Eversheds' Litigation and Dispute Resolution Partner, James Hyde, and Associate Neil Jackson about a recent case where the court considered who should bear the cost when hackers strike.

Mark Pearson is the founder of the website myvouchercodes.co.uk, which he outsourced for £300 and recently sold for £55 million. He still works on the site but also advises, and invests in, new companies. He spoke to Henry Tucker MBCS about it.

Enterprise resource planning (ERP) implementation methodologies have evolved over the years to cover all possible aspects of an implementation project, but they have not necessarily kept up with developments in the ERP packages themselves. The result is often quite cumbersome procedures that protect the implementation partner yet do little to facilitate the customer project requirements and often lengthen timescales, which results in restricted functionality in the final delivered project says Kevin Harmon-Smith.
One of the ways in which companies can grow is to join an accelerator. Toby Kress runs the London Accelerator. He spoke to Henry Tucker MBCS about it.

articleTitle: Untangling the Rat King IT and the Changing Legal Landscape
abstract: IT systems are global, becoming ever more social and are (at least in part) driven by big data. The IT market has shifted into true converged tech and corporate heavyweights who would have been unlikely bed-fellows in years gone by are cosying up to corner markets. As a result the legal landscape and its attendant issues are becoming even more complex, resembling the folkloric rat king - a whole bunch of rats irrevocably tangled together by their tails. Brian Runciman MBCS (with thanks to Charlotte Walker-Osborn, Head of Tech, Media and Telecoms at Eversheds LLP and a committee member of BCS-ISSG) delves further.

In addition to Donald Rumsfeld's much quoted ‘known unknowns’ and ‘unknown unknowns’ there’s another class of misapprehension that he failed to recognise - things you’re convinced of that happen to be wrong (in his case, WMD). For many of us in corporate information assurance, the real nature of risk is in this category. We all perform what we believe to be ‘risk assessments’, but Mike Barwise asks, are they really any good?

BCS, The Chartered Institute for IT, recently ran a live webinar about the IT skills gap. On the panel were Chris Shaw IT Director Sales and Marketing EMEA and Asia from Intel; Sarah Hill CEO and Founder from Capability Jane and Philip Black, COO from Emrgn. Brian Runciman MBCS chaired and reports.
Dr Justin Whatling, Chair BCS Health, Gwyn Thomas, Chair UKchip and Isabel Chevis, CEO IHRIM, explain their latest collaboration, namely a new federation for the health informatics profession.

articleTitle: Skills for the IT Team of the Future
abstract: The list of new and increasingly mainstream technologies and approaches is large: augmented reality, cognitive computing, 3D printing, the multiple uses of the cloud, the mobile workforce using app-driven devices, offshoring, onshoring, re-shoring. How will the IT team of future deal with these changes? What skills will they need? Brian Runciman MBCS reports on a recent BCS debate ‘The IT team of the future’.
When it comes to developing tools and products there are ethical things that you should consider say Bernd Carsten Stahl FBCS, Marina Jirotka, Grace Eden, Job Timmermans and Mark Hartswood.

Gillian Arnold, Director of Tectra and Chair of BCSWomen; Sue Sumner, Director of Global Finance Technology & Solutions at Barclays; and Rebecca George who is a Partner at Delloite, a BCS Trustee and the Chair of the Policy and Public Affairs Board at BCS debated the issues women face in IT in front of a live audience. Brian Runciman MBCS hosted and reports.

The term strong PMO is traditionally used to describe a model where the project or programme management office is deeply embedded in an organisation and acts as the central guiding authority on how programmes and their projects are to be managed. Here Dr Stefan Bertschi is using the term is to propose an organisational concept of strong PMO equally suitable for managing smaller projects that require a higher level of assurance.

In order to do business you need to place trust in others. By relaxing security and promoting trust, organisations can manage risk in a way that is more conducive to working practices according to Martin Gill from Perpetuity Research and Stephen Crane and Philipp Reinecke from Hewlett-Packard Labs.

Information security used to be simple. We locked doors, bolted windows, and that was sufficient. We took our cues for IT security architecture design from the same places, castles, walls, defence in depth, onion models, and network security based models positioned against external attack. These risks are not entirely the whole story says Ralph O'Brien MBCS.
David Galsworthy, CEO TechSpace, and Alex Rabarts, CTO TechSpace, spoke to Henry Tucker MBCS about the co-working space they co-founded and run in London.
